invariants.rationale: It is common practice to check for null before invoking a method, as seen in the body, so it's often expected that cell is either null or it has a non-null tile to be rendered.
Tilemap renderers usually use non-negative coordinates; enforcing this may reduce rendering glitches or out-of-bounds issues.
Similarly, y is likely non-negative in tiled map position context.
Colors are often represented in normalized floats between 0 and 1 in rendering pipelines.
Method immediately returns if the tile is an instance of AnimatedTiledMapTile; so, if cell is non-null, it is common for the tile not to be animated at point of rendering.
